inputs.label: Application repository
inputs.what: The GitHub OWNER/REPO that contains your mobile application, for example your-team/your-app.
inputs.why: The app checks your access to this one repository. It is separate from the Mobile Release Kit toolkit repository used by workflow templates.
inputs.where: Open your application's repository on GitHub. Copy the owner and repository names from github.com/OWNER/REPO, without the URL.
inputs.format: Exactly OWNER/REPO, at most 140 ASCII bytes; the existing core repository grammar applies. No branch, URL, host override or trailing slash.
inputs.failure: Invalid input is refused. A missing or inaccessible repository is not proof that it does not exist. Changing the target retires the original session; no automatic reconnection occurs.

inputs.label: Advanced session-only user token
inputs.what: An optional advanced alternative to Sign in with GitHub, available only when the installed native connection is qualified.
inputs.why: Use it if publisher device sign-in is unavailable or your organization requires a separately created user token. The app keeps it only for this session.
inputs.where: GitHub Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Fine-grained tokens. Select the application repository and Metadata/Actions read access for ordinary observations. The optional environment input check also needs Environments read access. Never put a token in project configuration, chat or a repository field.
inputs.format: Nonempty printable ASCII, at most 4096 bytes, without whitespace. Paste only into the gated password field. The app does not trim it, infer permissions from its prefix, import it from a file or store it on disk.
inputs.failure: A missing native profile or help resource disables entry before collection. Unauthorized requires a new deliberate sign-in after Disconnect settles. Forbidden can reflect repository, organization or SSO policy; do not automatically request broader access.

guidance.label: Sign in with GitHub
guidance.what: The app requests a short code and opens GitHub's device verification page. You sign in and approve access on GitHub, never enter your GitHub password in this app.
guidance.why: The code links this original desktop session to the publisher's registered GitHub App. Receiving a token is not yet a successful connection: the app must also check account and repository identity.
guidance.where: Click Sign in with GitHub, then Open GitHub, or visit https://github.com/login/device yourself. Enter the displayed code and check that GitHub shows the same publisher name before approving.
guidance.format: The displayed code looks like AB12-CD34. Copy it exactly into GitHub, not into project configuration. One sign-in lasts at most 15 minutes; the app waits and polls automatically at GitHub's allowed interval.
guidance.failure: Publisher-unconfigured means the publisher must register/enable device flow; not-qualified means this installed native path is not available. A lost reply does not authorize another sign-in. Use Status and Cancel, then wait for the original cleanup.

guidance.label: Repository access and organization approval
guidance.what: The publisher App requests Metadata read, Contents read and Actions write for the supported observation and explicitly confirmed workflow actions.
guidance.why: Authentication alone does not guarantee access. The App installation, your account and your organization's approval must all allow the selected repository. Actions write is not permission for an automatic release.
guidance.where: Ask a repository or organization administrator to install/approve the publisher App for the selected application repository. Check GitHub Settings > Applications and the organization's installed GitHub Apps if access is pending.
guidance.format: Choose only the repositories you intend to manage. Reported pull/push/admin roles are separate observations, not proof of effective token scope or environment approval. Secret values and repository settings are not read by sign-in. A separate input-metadata check needs Environments read access; an unavailable grant is reported, never expanded automatically.
guidance.failure: 401 means unauthorized; 403 may mean organization/SSO or App permission policy; 404 means missing or inaccessible. Follow your organization's approval process rather than widening permissions automatically.

guidance.label: Session-only lifetime and original settlement
guidance.what: The native app retains one credential only in private session memory. Device codes and refresh tokens are never public status, project files, logs, history or credential assets.
guidance.why: Sign-in does not need persistent credential storage or an unlocked keyring. Refresh tokens are discarded, so this session cannot silently renew authentication.
guidance.where: Use Disconnect or Cancel in the GitHub screen. Project/target changes, document loss, expiry and shutdown also retire the original consumers.
guidance.format: The credential ceiling is 60 minutes from the original sign-in admission, including time spent approving the device code. Known expiry only shortens it. Status, Refresh, input-metadata checks, navigation and clock changes do not extend it.
guidance.failure: Cleanup-unknown stays visible and blocks new work even after a late response. A click, closed screen or lost reply is not proof of native cleanup or complete memory erasure; keep the original app open for settlement.

guidance.label: Bind the original immutable identities
guidance.what: Account, repository and remote workflow IDs are canonical positive decimal strings, not lossy JavaScript numbers.
guidance.why: A renamed, replaced or recreated target must not silently inherit the original observation or credential admission.
guidance.where: The native owner keeps the original account/repository IDs and checks repository identity before and after workflow listing or a separately requested environment input observation. The UI shows only the accepted safe observations.
guidance.format: After authentication, at most five fixed HTTPS reads check account, repository and two workflow pages. There are no redirects, automatic read retries or returned-URL following. A device token is not shown as connected before these checks settle.
guidance.failure: Target-changed refuses new identity adoption. Network-unavailable, TLS-failed, response-invalid and response-limit are fixed local failures, never raw response text or a suggestion to disable TLS.

guidance.label: Workflow metadata is not local-file verification
guidance.what: The four core-owned workflow IDs may be listed, not-listed or unknown, with active, disabled or unknown remote state.
guidance.why: Not-listed means only not returned by a complete bounded Actions listing. It says nothing about Git file absence, YAML compatibility, approvals or release readiness.
guidance.where: Compare this section with Local workflow files without merging their claims. Repository Actions settings/policy, protections and runners remain unobserved. The separate Environment inputs section observes one field's metadata only; it does not verify values, workflow contents or readiness.
guidance.format: Exactly four rows in the existing core roster order. Incomplete coverage cannot report not-listed. Duplicate/changing listings become limited/unknown, not a complete snapshot.
guidance.failure: Rate-limited has no automatic retry. After a lost reply, inspect original Status rather than repeating Connect/Refresh. A later explicit read requires actual original settlement and native cooldown admission.

guidance.label: Sign-in is not permission to release
guidance.what: The connection screen observes GitHub. Local workflow Apply is a separate transaction and does not push files. Supported workflow dispatches use their own reviewed preview and explicit confirmation.
guidance.why: A login does not approve a workflow run, bypass a protected environment or authorize a Store mutation. Build-once, provenance, recovery and release safeguards still apply.
guidance.where: Use the separate workflow/release screen for an available action. Review its exact repository, immutable target, environment and effects before confirmation.
guidance.format: The connection status keeps remote mutation/dispatch false and release readiness unknown. Other action screens have independent capability and one-use consent contracts; no general remote setup or secret readback is granted.
guidance.failure: An ambiguous action must reconcile its original operation, never repeat a dispatch or adopt the latest run. Cancelling local sign-in does not cancel a remote workflow or revoke its GitHub grant.

guidance.label: Local Disconnect is not remote revocation
guidance.what: Disconnect requests local retirement and cancellation of the exact original session, even while an observation is busy.
guidance.why: Remote grants remain controlled by GitHub. Starting a new login does not revoke an older token or grant.
guidance.where: To revoke App access remotely, use GitHub Settings > Applications > Authorized GitHub Apps and select the publisher App. For an advanced token, use Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens. Organization installations may require an administrator.
guidance.format: The Open GitHub button opens only https://github.com/login/device for the current waiting sign-in. It cannot open a supplied URL. Cancel stops local sign-in and clears the displayed code; Disconnect retires the original local session.
guidance.failure: Failed or expired device sign-in cannot be refreshed or automatically restarted. Wait for Disconnect/Cancel to settle, then explicitly start a new sign-in. Cleanup-unknown is not cleared by a new token or late success.
